headline: Craze & Crash keeps viewers with rivalry, break-up and myth stories and loses them with founder-money hooks; 94% of its views come from the Shorts feed.

working.text: Hooks that are not a starting-money figure (conflict, myth, question): 50.8% stayed to watch on average (5 Shorts).
Ledger music: 49.1% stayed (4 Shorts) with a median of 1,258 views in 48 hours.

notWorking.text: Shock-number hooks about a founder's small start (Nike's $35, Dollar Shave Club's $4,500, Spanx's $5,000): 26.7% stayed (3 Shorts), 24 points under the rest.
Dossier music: 34.5% stayed (4 Shorts), median 62 views in 48 hours; 3 of those 4 also had the shock-number hook, so the hook may be the cause.

audience.text: The United States gives 68.5% of Shorts views over 28 days, and watches 72.3% of each on average; India 4.5% at 51%.
Men 35 to 44 are the largest group (19% of views), then men 45 to 54 (15.9%).
79.7% of views are on phones and 15.2% on tablets.
94.3% of Shorts views come from the Shorts feed and 4.3% from search (top search: tamagotchi, 30% of search views).

recommendations.do: Open on a rivalry, a break-up or a myth rather than a founder's starting money.
recommendations.because: Shock-number founder hooks averaged 26.7% stayed (3 Shorts) against 50.8% for the other hooks (5 Shorts).

recommendations.do: Pick famous brand names that people search for (Krispy Kreme, Tamagotchi) and put them first in the title.
recommendations.because: 4.3% of views come from search, and tamagotchi and krispy kreme are the two top searches (30% and 17.1% of search views).

recommendations.do: Write for an American adult audience: US prices, US brands, plain English.
recommendations.because: 68.5% of views come from the United States, which watches 72.3% of each Short against 51% in India.
